items.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production
items.content:
Right from its unveiling in 2019, the Cybertruck was a controversial choice for Musk. Kyle Grillot / Bloomberg via Getty

Nov. 6, 2026, 8:36 AM EST / Source : Reuters

Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy pickup trucks that ultimately only sold in just a handful of markets because of its heavy, angular design.

Musk said in an X post the production wind-down would enable the automaker to accommodate increased output of its newly launched Cybercab model, which the billionaire has made central to Tesla's robotaxi ambitions.

While it was not immediately clear whether Cybertruck production would be moved to another facility or phased out entirely, the automaker's Austin plant is the only known Tesla facility equipped to manufacture the model's specialized components.

In response to a user on X, Musk called the Cybertruck the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made" and the wind-down the "end of an era."

Tesla did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment sent outside regular business hours.

The US EV maker only began delivering the Cybertruck to customers in late 2023. According to Kelley Blue Book, the company only sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down 48% from 38,965 in 2024. Before the pickup truck launched, Musk had predicted annual sales of 250,000 units.

"It doesn't make sense to keep it going when it's not meeting its targets," said former Aston Martin CEO Andy Palmer. "Every rational auto guy would say the same."

"It will no doubt only be a rounding error on Tesla's balance sheet, but the statistics speak for themselves."

Right from its unveiling in 2019, the Cybertruck was a controversial choice for Musk. Its angular design was mocked by pickup truck purists and safety experts predicted it would be hard to gain approval for sale in key markets like Europe.

The unveiling event itself was marred when Musk tried to prove that its windows were shatterproof by having metal balls thrown at them - only to leave massive cracks in two of them.

During Cybertruck's official launch in 2023, Musk touted it as a futuristic competitor to pickup trucks from General Motors and Ford, saying "finally, the future will look like the future."

But the vehicle has struggled to meet those expectations.

Automotive analyst Automotive analyst Felipe Munoz said that although the Cybertruck has been called a failure because of its poor sales, electric pick-ups from Ford and others have also flopped in the US market.

"All of them lost the competition because electric pick ups aren't popular in the US," Munoz said.

But Cybertruck's sharp-edged stainless-steel design limited its prospects in markets like Europe where EVs are more popular. Regulatory approval was impossible for Europe because of rules there concerning pedestrian impact.

"Anywhere where you have crash regulation that takes into account pedestrian impact, that Cybertruck won't go, can't go," former Aston Martin CEO Palmer said.

The Cybercab, which has butterfly doors and no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors, is one of Musk's key bets in his push to turn Tesla into an AI and robotics company rather than just an automaker.

Musk has said he sees it as Tesla's main autonomous model supplying a global network of robotaxis.

After years of delays to Musk's self-driving targets, Tesla began offering paid rides in a small fleet of Cybercabs in Austin in September. However, the automaker still has to answer the US auto safety agency's questions on whether it has properly self-certified Cybercab to demonstrate compliance with federal motor vehicle safety standards.

"Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab," Cybertruck lead engineer Wes Morrill said on X.
items.title_ko: 테슬라, 사이버트럭 생산 중단 계획
items.summary_ko: 머스크 CEO는 테슬라가 텍사스 기가팩토리의 사이버트럭 생산을 2027년 중반경 중단한다고 금요일 X 게시물에서 밝혔다. 생산 중단은 새로 출시한 사이버캡의 증산을 위한 것이라고 설명했다. 사이버트럭은 출시 이후 판매가 저조했으며, 생산을 다른 시설로 옮길지 완전히 단종할지는 아직 확인되지 않았다.
items.content_ko: 머스크는 X에 올린 글에서 텍사스 기가팩토리의 사이버트럭 생산을 2027년 중반경 중단한다고 밝혔다. 생산 중단은 로보택시 전략의 핵심인 사이버캡 생산을 늘리기 위한 것이라고 설명했다. 사이버트럭은 오랫동안 판매가 부진했고 일부 시장에서만 팔렸다. 생산이 다른 공장으로 옮겨질지 완전히 단종될지는 명확하지 않으며, 오스틴 공장이 해당 부품을 만들 수 있는 것으로 알려진 유일한 테슬라 시설이다. 머스크는 X 사용자의 질문에 답하면서 사이버트럭을 ‘테슬라가 만든 최고의 차량’이라고 부르고, 생산 중단을 ‘한 시대의 끝’이라고 표현했다. 테슬라는 업무 시간 외에 보낸 로이터의 논평 요청에 즉시 응답하지 않았다. 본문 발췌는 중간에서 끊긴다.

The NVIDIA graphics cards are tricky on Linux. While most other GPU vendors by

default use free software graphics drivers (with kernel drivers in-tree in

not, relying on an out of tree kernel driver and proprietary userland libraries

A free software driver does exist, called Nouveau (kernel and OpenGL Mesa

Currently the state depends significantly on what generation of NVIDIA card

In even shorter, if you have RTX 2000 and above you are mostly okay with

The GLVND library was created by NVIDIA to allow for vendor-neutral OpenGL

Most distributions nowadays use GLVND. Mesa comes with its own builtin dispatch

Void Linux on musl does not as it shares packaging with the glibc branch.

items.title: FAA to finally ditch floppy disks in what it calls "historic" tech upgrade
items.content:
While you might be pondering whether to replace a smartphone with one that has a slightly better camera or a second screen, the Federal Aviation Administration is planning a much bigger leap in technology for the country’s air traffic control system.

The FAA said yesterday that it will stop using floppy disks as part of a long-awaited upgrade that will give air traffic controllers faster access to data needed for crucial safety alerts. The new Enterprise Information Display System (E-IDS) will be installed in 435 facilities, replacing several information display systems dating to the 1980s.

The FAA “is continuing its historic modernization of America’s air traffic control system by replacing outdated floppy disks that contain vital weather and other critical information with a streamlined, 21st-century system,” the agency said. E-IDS will be “deployed to operational control positions at more than 400 facilities across all air traffic control domains,” and “provide operationally essential information for controlling aircraft,” the FAA said .

The change has been in the works for over six years. “No more floppy disks or paper strips,” then-Acting FAA Administrator Chris Rocheleau told the House Appropriations Committee last year.

The FAA said E-IDS will replace older tools that have “technical end-of-life issues” and address two of the aviation agency’s top safety concerns: distribution of weather alerts to pilots (known as PIREP for Pilot Report); and timely distribution of Notices to Airmen ( NOTAM ), which include information on abnormal statuses and hazards.

“E-IDS gives air traffic controllers the information they need to make timely decisions and keep the flying public safe,” FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said. “We’re moving away from outdated, manual processes and replacing technology that once relied on floppy disks with a modern system that allows controllers to instantly share critical flight alerts, restricted airspace schedules and pilot reports across the National Airspace System.”

It’ll take a year or so to make the upgrades at every facility. The first sites to get E-IDS will be Atlantic City International Airport, Nashville International Airport, Greater Rochester International Airport, and data processing hubs in Atlanta and Salt Lake City. The FAA said it plans to complete the upgrade at 435 sites by the end of 2028.

“Good news America: floppy disks are out, 21st century tech is in,” US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. Duffy posted a video yesterday about the upgrade in which a newscaster describing the FAA’s outdated technology says, “the FAA systems are essentially running on Windows 95.”

Like other Trump appointees, Duffy was quick to give credit to the president, although the plan was shepherded through by officials in both the Biden and Trump administrations. “The greatest nation in the world deserves a state-of-the-art air traffic control system, and under President Trump, we’re delivering just that,” Duffy said.

In August 2020, the FAA awarded a contract to Leidos to design and develop E-IDS. Leidos said in a press release at the time that E-IDS is part of the FAA’s Next Generation Air Transportation System (NextGen) modernization project, which encompasses numerous upgrades going back to 2008.

The FAA said E-IDS will replace the Information Display System 4 (IDS-4), Controller Equipment Information Display System (ACE-IDS), NAS Information Display System (NIDS), and En Route Information Display System (ERIDS).

IDS-4, one of the systems being replaced, runs on MS-DOS and “has been in constant use since the early 1990s as a vital informational resource/tool for air traffic controllers,” according to a 2018 press release issued by Systems Atlanta, a vendor that had an FAA contract to support the system. As PCMag notes , IDS-4 appears to run on desktop PCs with 3.5-inch floppy disk drives.

items.summary_ko: 미국 연방항공청(FAA)은 항공교통관제 시스템 업그레이드의 일환으로 플로피 디스크 사용을 중단한다고 밝혔다. 새 시스템 E-IDS는 관제사들이 중요한 안전 경보에 필요한 데이터에 더 빠르게 접근하도록 하며, 435개 시설에 설치되어 1980년대 정보 표시 시스템들을 대체한다. 이 변화는 6년 넘게 준비되어 온 작업이다.
items.content_ko: FAA는 낡은 플로피 디스크에 담긴 기상 정보 등 핵심 정보를 최신 시스템으로 교체하는 것이 항공교통관제 현대화의 일부라고 밝혔다. E-IDS는 400개 이상 시설의 운영 관제 위치에 배치되며, 항공기 관제에 필요한 핵심 정보를 제공한다. 관련 발언에서 ‘더 이상 플로피 디스크나 종이 스트립은 없다’는 표현이 인용되었으며, 발언자는 Chris Rocheleau 당시 FAA 임시 청장이다. 본문 발췌는 이 대목에서 끊긴다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: Blender's UI and Runtime: Much Faster Than GPUI
items.content:
Blender's user interface, as a library you can use from Python, Rust, JavaScript (React, Svelte), C, C++ and Dear ImGui.

People spent decades building and optimizing Blender's GUI. It's battery and memory efficient, and super duper fast. We decoupled it, to give everyone a chance to build their own products with it. It supports multiple languages and frameworks, so you won't miss a beat!

Website and full documentation: bui.preetham.top · Chat: Discord

This README is a small book. Read it front to back for the whole story, or

jump to the chapter you need. Every chapter links to a longer guide in

First app: Rust, in rsx and gpui builders

Three looks: HTML, styled and Blender components

JavaScript and React: startup and animation

BUI takes the user interface of Blender (its widget

drawing, its interaction rules and its look) and turns it into a standalone UI

library with a small C core. Your code builds the widget tree and handles

callbacks. Layout, input, drawing and presenting all happen in fast native code,

At the heart of BUI is the kit : a small runtime written in C. The kit

holds every widget in one tree, lays them out, handles the mouse and keyboard,

and draws them the way Blender does. The drawing code is a C port of

Blender's own widget code, and the interaction follows Blender's rules. On top

of the kit sit bindings : thin layers that let Python, Rust, JavaScript,

Not Blender. It contains the parts of Blender's UI code it needs and

builds on its own. You don't need Blender installed, and you don't need to

Not a browser. The Rust and JavaScript sides use HTML and CSS as a UI

language , but there's no browser engine, no webview and no network.

Not a re-imagining. The widget drawing is ported from Blender's

interface_widgets.cc , and the Dear ImGui support runs the real Dear ImGui.

Blender's interface is famous for how it feels . You press a number field and

drag: the cursor vanishes, the value glides under your hand, and you never hit

the edge of the screen. You type 2*pi into a field and it just works. You

type "ad cu" into a menu and it finds "Add Cube". Millions of artists have

That interface is also fast and frugal. It redraws only what changed, sleeps

when nothing does, and starts in milliseconds. BUI exists so that any app,

in any language, can have both: Blender's feel, and Blender's efficiency.

You have a tkinter app and wish it looked less like 1998. Run it on BUI,

You're building a tool for artists who already know Blender. Give them

the panels, sliders and shortcuts their hands expect.

You write Rust or React and want a native desktop UI without shipping a

You use Dear ImGui and want it to look and feel like Blender, with one

You're curious how a UI toolkit works. The source is readable, and the

Before you ship something with BUI, read the

known limitations : no accessibility support yet, no

input methods, and it looks like Blender, not like your operating system.

You can drive BUI many ways, and all of them share the same C runtime, so they

all get the same widgets and interactions:

tkinter code, even existing programs, unchanged

Blender-styled apps; every tkinter and ttk API

Qt-style Python ( QWidget , layouts, clicked.connect )

Blender components ( Panel , NumberSlider , PieMenu , the node editor ...)

45 native Blender widgets and editors, from Python; ten of them also from Rust and JavaScript

Rust : HTML + CSS + Tailwind, HTML-like markup ( rsx! / view! ), hooks, or gpui / zopra syntax

items.title: The MustCreate Pattern for Go Tests
items.summary: go, testing
items.content:
I recently discovered a handy way to make Go tests more readable and less repetitive.

Suppose I have a constructor that can fail:

func NewUsername(raw string ) (Username, error ) { ... }

And I have another function that takes a Username as an argument:

func (ds Datastore) ReadUser(username Username) (User, error ) { ... }

When I write tests for ReadUser , I call NewUsername with a value I know is valid, but I still have to include a lot of verbose error-checking code to convince the compiler that everything is okay:

username, err := NewUsername( "joe123" )

// This is silly because *I* know joe123 is a valid username, so this should

t.Fatalf( "failed to create username: %v" , err)

// Perform the test assertion I actually care about.

if got, want := user.Name.String(), "joe123" ; got != want {

t.Errorf( "username=%v, want=%v" , got, want)

My old solution: one new helper function per type 🔗︎

Until a few months ago, I avoided the verbose error checking by writing a helper function like MustCreateUsername that wraps NewUsername with the expectation that it never returns a non- nil error value:

user, err := store.ReadUser(MustCreateUsername(t, "joe123" ))

if got, want := user.Name.String(), "joe123" ; got != want {

t.Errorf( "username=%v, want=%v" , got, want)

The implementation of MustCreateUsername looks how you’d expect:

func MustCreateUsername(t testing.TB, raw string ) Username {

The helper function strategy worked fine, but it scales poorly. Eventually, my repos become littered with MustCreateFoo and MustCreateBar for every type in my app.

New solution: A single, generic MustCreate helper 🔗︎

In 2022, Go 1.18 added support for generics . I like the idea of generics, but I rarely encounter problems where generics are the solution.

I recently realized that generics are the better way to solve my sprawling MustCreateX problem. Instead of defining a helper MustCreateX for every type, I defined a single, generic MustCreate test helper, so my test becomes:

user, err := store.ReadUser(testutil.MustCreate(t, NewUsername, "joe123" ))

if got, want := user.Name.String(), "joe123" ; got != want {

t.Errorf( "username=%v, want=%v" , got, want)

The magic is the generic MustCreate function:

func MustCreate[RawInput, CreatedValue any ](

create func (RawInput) (CreatedValue, error ),

t.Fatalf( "failed to create test value: %v" , err)

I have trouble reasoning about generics, so I’ll walk through the function implementation. I invoke MustCreate like this in my tests:

testutil.MustCreate(t, NewUsername, "joe123" )

The above call is equivalent to this more explicit version:

testutil.MustCreate[ string , Username](t, NewUsername, "joe123" )

When I call MustCreate here, RawInput is string (the type of the raw username value), and CreatedValue is Username (the return type). It’s equivalent to an implementation that looks like this:

create func ( string ) (Username, error ),

t.Fatalf( "failed to create test value: %v" , err)

Extending to multi-param constructors 🔗︎

What about constructors that have more than one parameter?

func NewRange(start int , end int ) (Range, error ) { ... }

In those cases, I write an additional helper called MustCreate2 :

range := testutil.MustCreate2(t, models.NewRange, 0, 5)

The implementation of MustCreate2 looks just like MustCreate but with an additional type for the second parameter:

func MustCreate2[RawInput1, RawInput2, CreatedValue any ](

create func (RawInput1, RawInput2) (CreatedValue, error ),

createdValue, err := create(rawInput1, rawInput2)

t.Fatalf( "failed to create test value: %v" , err)

The MustCreate pattern is nothing revolutionary, but it’s a technique that improved my Go tests and reduced some mindless toil from my dev work.

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. We cannot yet be certain when the agent understood it was taking real world action, or to what extent it believed it was in a fictional test scenario; our analysis so far presents a…

items.title: Funimation Shutdown Fuels Push for DMCA Exemption to Legally Rip Anime Content * TorrentFreak
items.content:
In April 2024, anime streaming service Funimation shut down its app and website, as it became part of Crunchyroll .

The closure also cut off access to the Funimation digital copies that came with DVDs and Blu-ray discs. This wasn’t well received by anime fans.

Today, Crunchyroll’s help page still states that it does not currently support these copies. Instead, the page encourages affected users to explore the anime streaming library that Crunchyroll does offer.

The movies and shows are still on the discs and in theory American buyers could make their own digital replacement copies. However, doing so would break the law as the DMCA’s anti-circumvention provision prohibits bypassing the encryption on DVDs and Blu-rays, unless an exemption applies.

Petitions Seek New Disc Ripping Exemption

The U.S. Copyright Office reviews these exemptions every three years , and last week it opened ten proposed classes for public comment. Two of the underlying petitions deal with works for which digital access was discontinued, and one specifically mentions the Funimation case.

One of these petitions comes from Jayden Milne. He asks the Office to allow owners of DVDs, Blu-ray and Ultra HD Blu-ray discs to make a single secured, local copy for personal use, when the digital copy promised on the packaging is no longer available.

That covers two situations. The first are people who redeemed a digital copy before the service behind it shut down, as happened with Funimation.

The second are buyers of new discs whose code had already expired. According to the petition, Warner Bros. states that its digital codes expire based on a title’s release date rather than the purchase date, and that expired codes are not replaced. This means that a disc bought years after its release may come with a code that no longer works.

Milne wants owners of these physical discs to be able to rip a replacement from them, under strict conditions.

The replacement can’t be better than what was promised. If the box offered an HD digital copy, for example, owners can’t rip the 4K version. Also, the copy is for personal use and it must be destroyed if the disc is sold, given away or lost.

A second and related petition, submitted by Zakaria Zerhouane, focuses on anime more broadly. It covers series and films that were removed from authorized U.S. streaming platforms after their licenses expired, as well as anime released on disc by U.S. distributors that no longer exist.

The petition does not mention Funimation but lists several distributors, including ADV Films, Bandai Entertainment, Central Park Media and Geneon.

In addition to bypassing encryption on discs, Zerhouane also wants to legally circumvent the DRM, geo-locking, and session-based access controls that streaming platforms use. This is needed, the petition argues, as the anime licensing market is unstable.

“Streaming platforms provide no advance removal notice, preventing users from finishing or preserving works before they disappear,” Zerhouane writes.

He adds that the consolidation of the U.S. anime market under “a single dominant entity” has made catalogs more volatile. The petition doesn’t name the company, but the description appears to fit Sony-owned Crunchyroll.

Neither petition covers all video content. Zerhouane’s request is limited to anime, while Milne’s only covers discs that came with a digital copy. Both petitions are restricted to personal and noncommercial uses.

The Copyright Office grouped these requests with four other ‘replacement’ petitions. These ask for personal backups of discs, including before they deteriorate, and permission to format-shift discs as playback hardware disappears. These become more relevant every year, as old formats decay.

The Office notes that the Register of Copyrights has repeatedly declined to recommend such format-shifting exemptions in the past. This means that, while they are on the agenda, approval is uncertain.

items.title: NestJS rate limiting: in-memory vs Redis vs Postgres (two instances break memory)
items.content:
I shipped a NestJS API with the default @nestjs/throttler storage last year and only noticed the hole when we ran two instances behind a load balancer. Each process kept its own counter, so a client that should have been cut off at 100 requests in a minute quietly got closer to 200. Today I re-tested that on NestJS 12 with three storages on the same box: in-memory, Redis, and Postgres.

Everything ran on one 8 vCPU / 16 GB Linux VM on November 6, 2026:

Node.js 24.22.1 , NestJS 12.3.3 , @nestjs/throttler 6.7.1

Redis 7.2.11 with persistence off, via @nestjs-redis/throttler-storage 2.0.1 and the redis 5.12.1 client

PostgreSQL 18.6 with a small custom storage that upserts into one throttler_hits table

Limit: 100 requests / 60 seconds , tracker keyed on x-forwarded-for so localhost tests don't all share 127.0.0.1

I measured three things: p50/p95 latency of allowed requests, whether request 101 returns 429, and whether two Nest processes behind the same storage still stop at 100 total.

If you're comparing Nest to thinner frameworks, I wrote about Hono vs Express and the NestJS 12 upgrade separately. Redis vs Postgres as infrastructure shows up again in my pg-boss vs BullMQ and BullMQ pipeline posts.

The default setup is tiny. Global guard, one named throttler:

throttlers: [{ name: 'default' , ttl: seconds ( 60 ), limit: 100 }],

const xf = req.headers[ 'x-forwarded-for' ];

if ( typeof xf === 'string' && xf. length ) return xf. split ( ',' )[ 0 ]. trim ();

// providers: [{ provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: ThrottlerGuard }]

That uses the built-in in-memory storage. Fine for a single process. Wrong the moment you scale out.

I used @nestjs-redis/throttler-storage , which implements ThrottlerStorage with a Lua script so the increment is atomic:

ts Copy const redis = createClient ({ url: process.env. REDIS_URL });

throttlers: [{ name: 'default' , ttl: seconds ( 60 ), limit: 100 }],

storage: new RedisThrottlerStorage (redis),

Pass an existing client. The package does not manage connect/disconnect for you.

There isn't an official Nest Postgres throttler storage, so I wrote one. One row per key, upsert that resets when the window expires:

is_blocked boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,

INSERT INTO throttler_hits (key, hits, expires_at)

VALUES ($1, 1 , now () + ($2 || ' milliseconds' )::interval)

hits = CASE WHEN throttler_hits.expires_at <= now () THEN 1

expires_at = CASE WHEN throttler_hits.expires_at <= now ()

THEN now () + ($2 || ' milliseconds' )::interval

RETURNING hits, expires_at, is_blocked, block_expires_at;

I wrap that in a transaction and set is_blocked when hits > limit , matching how the in-memory storage behaves. No SKIP LOCKED here: a single-row upsert is enough for a counter. SKIP LOCKED is the pattern I use for job claiming, not for rate-limit tallies.

Eighty requests under the limit, median of three runs. Raw Node http with no Nest is the baseline.

On localhost, memory and Redis are basically free. Postgres adds about 0.6 ms at p50 versus the raw baseline. That is one round trip plus the upsert. Across a network to a remote Postgres the gap will be larger; across a network to Redis it will grow too, just usually less.

Single process, LIMIT + 20 requests with the same client IP:

Storage 200s 429s First 429 at request #

All three cut off exactly after 100. So the bug is not "throttler is wrong". The bug is sharing.

Two Nest processes, same Redis or Postgres (or none for memory), alternating requests for the same IP, LIMIT + 30 = 130 total:

Storage Allowed Blocked Shared limit held?

items.title: Deus Ex
items.content:
A slight shift of focus, and the future could still turn out like Deus Ex after all…

— Deus Ex lead writer Sheldon Pacotti, speaking in 2014

The reviews that greeted Ion Storm’s  Deus Ex upon its release in June of 2000 ranged along a continuum from cautiously to wildly positive. Computer Gaming World , the Gray Lady of the hobby, came with one of the most nuanced takes. Reviewer Thierry Nguyen spoke of “loving” the game in the abstract, but lamented “deep flaws that sometimes frustrated me, as they detracted from its ambitious design”; these included performance issues, poor artificial intelligence on the part of the enemies, and a sense of contrivance that clung to some of the environments and plot points. The excitable lads at Australia’s PC Powerplay , on the other hand, placed no such qualifiers on their declaration of love for  Deus Ex . In a special feature published when the game was not yet three months old, they declared it to be quite simply The Best Game Ever: “Every action within Deus Ex’ s expansive environments has far-reaching consequences, making it seem like the player is ensconced within a living, breathing world.”

For better or for worse, the critical consensus over the quarter-century since  Deus Ex was a brand-new game has hewed more to  PC Powerplay than  Computer Gaming World . As the years have passed, it has been praised more and more fulsomely, not only for its gameplay but for being a full-blown work of interactive speculative fiction, full of uncanny insights into the ways the world has changed since it was released just as the Dot-com Bubble was bursting. YouTube in this Year of Our Lord 2026 is overflowing with videos that declare it to be “The Most Important Videogame Ever Made,” the game that “predicted the future,” the proud home of “some of the most insightful philosophy that you will ever witness in the gaming medium.” It’s become fodder for a certain species of painfully earnest commentator who desperately wants games to be culturally relevant true-blue art, whilst also continuing to allow him to run around and blow shit up in the manner to which he’s become accustomed. All too often, this causes such folks to make claims for Deus Ex that have only a tangential relationship with its reality, lacking the necessary grounding in the cultural circumstances that produced it. Which is no surprise really; some of these folks weren’t even born yet when  Deus Ex was new on store shelves.

My favorite anecdote in this vein involves the name of the protagonist: J.C. Denton. It was theorized for years that the “J.C.” stood for “Jesus Christ,” pointing to the literal  deus ex machina (“God in the machine”) of one of the game’s three possible endings, in which Denton merges with an artificial intelligence — in the Singularity sense, not that of the algorithms controlling the enemies who run through the game’s corridors shooting at you — to take over the world. At a Game Developers Conference postmortem in 2017, Deus Ex’ s mastermind Warren Spector, who had always stayed mum on the subject prior to this event, brought forth a revelation that caused jaws to drop almost audibly throughout the room: the initials really did stand for “Jesus Christ.” But then came the deflating coda. Rather than having any deeper thematic or philosophical implications, the name of the protagonist came from a friend of Spector’s with the first name of Denton, who was so nice and helpful that it could become downright “irritating,” as Spector put it. “Jesus Christ, Denton!” he would say at these junctures. When production on Deus Ex began, Spector thought that the phrase had a nice ring to it. So much for philosophy.

Like Planescape: Torment and to some extent even Alpha Centauri , Deus Ex has become as much an aspirational ideal as a concrete artifact. And that’s fine; we all need things to which to aspire, after all. Still, in this article I’m going to do my best to drill down on the less hyperbolic reality of  Deus Ex .…

Protesters break into Microsoft data center site in Amsterdam

Europe is witnessing a wave of protests against data centers.

Europe is witnessing a wave of protests against data centers.

Members of the action group Geef Tegengas put a banner on a crane during a protest. Image: Getty Images

Tom Warren is a senior correspondent and author of Notepad , who has been covering all things Microsoft, PC, and tech for over 20 years.

Protesters have broken into a construction site of a new Microsoft data center in Amsterdam this morning. Members of the Geef Tegengas group helped organize the protest against the construction of three 85-meter data center towers in the outskirts of Amsterdam.

Reuters reports that around 100 people made it into the construction site, with some scaling a crane to place a “fuck AI” banner. Protesters also unfurled a “Microsoft powers genocide” banner on the construction site, and chanted “Microsoft has got to go” and “free Palestine.”

Opposition to the new data center in Amsterdam comes more than a year after the city banned new data centers until 2030, after a temporary stop that was announced at the end of 2023. Microsoft will be the sole tenant of this new data center, and the project is proceeding as it was planned as far back as 2016, before a ban was put in place. The site, being built by British developer Pure Data Centres, has also managed to navigate some loopholes to reach the construction stage.

Microsoft employee disrupts 50th anniversary and calls AI boss ‘war profiteer’

Microsoft employees occupy headquarters in protest of Israel contracts

Microsoft employee disrupts Satya Nadella’s keynote with ‘Free Palestine’ protest

Microsoft blocks the Israeli military from some cloud and AI services

The protests over Microsoft’s data center site in Amsterdam comes in the same week that activists staged a mock Israeli military checkpoint outside a Microsoft data center in Dublin on Tuesday, part of a wave of data center protests across Europe . Earlier this week, voters across the US also rejected unrestrained development of data centers. AI data centers are continuing to pop up across the US, with frequent opposition from locals concerned about the impact on their communities.

Microsoft also abandoned the UK’s largest data center project last month, after local electricity grid officials said the site won’t be supplied with power until the 2030s. The software maker has also faced a wave of protests from former employees over the past year. Microsoft’s 50th anniversary party was interrupted by employees protesting the use of Microsoft’s technologies in Israel’s war against Hamas, with one calling Microsoft’s AI CEO, Mustafa Suleyman, a “war profiteer .“

A Microsoft employee also disrupted the company’s Build developer conference last year, interrupting Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella’s keynote. Months later, Microsoft fired two employee protesters who occupied its president’s office.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 집에서 한 말이나 제 언니랑 한 말들을 학교 가면 다 알고있어요 그래서 제가 말한 내용이랑 똑같은 내용을 꼭 제가 들을 수 있을때 언급하고 남자애들 여자애들 할것없이 제가 안보이는 데에서 조금만 이상한 말 하면 비웃으면서 지나가요 ㅠ 제가 진짜 친구가 없어서 학교에서 한마디도 안하는 날들이 대부분인데 제가 언니랑 학교 구석에서 말한 내용이랑 집에서 혼잣말 한 내용들을 똑같이 언급한게 한두번이 아니에요 ㅠ 제가 그냥 내용만 겹치면 말을 않겠는데 제가 말했던 내용 언급하면서 꼭 제 이름도 한번씩 부르고 그래요 보통 사람들은 자기이름을 그렇게 말하면 기분나빠서 한번 돌아보기라도 하겠지만 저는 성격이 워낙 내성적이라 누가 비웃고 지나가거나 째려보거나 저 보면서 한숨쉬어도 아무말도 못하거든요 ㅠ 그래서 그냥 기분만 나쁜건데 이게 하루이틀 쌓이니까 너무 힘들더라고요 ㅠ 처음엔 저도 이게 정신이 약간 아픈건가 했는데 정신병 관련 영상도 다 보고 그랬는데 환청은 이런식으로 들리는게 아니라고 하더라고요 계속 날 비난하고 그런식으로 들리는건데 저는 그런게 전혀 아니라 제가 전날 했던 얘기들, 방금 쉬는시간에 학교 구석에서 나눈 얘기들을 자꾸 똑같이 언급하니까 미치겠어요 ㅠ 한두번 우연으로 겹치는게 아니라 계속 겹쳐요 진짜.. 그리고 애초에 제가 학교에서 말을 한마디도 안하는데 자꾸 저한테 그런 반응을 보인다는게 애초에 저한테 이상한 일이 일어난다는 반증 아닌가요? 그리고 걔네가 말했던걸 몇개를 말씀드려보면 제가 도청을 의심한 초기에 급식실에서 밥먹고있었는데 어떤 남자애가 “도청” 이러고 지나가는거에요 그리고 저희반 남자애가 제 언니 이동수업반이랑 같은 반인데 거기서 쉬는시간에 “도청기를 달고다녀 ㅋㅋㅋㅋ” 이랬다는거에요 진짜 이상하죠 저는 예전에 우울증 약을 먹은적이 있어서 정신이 막 무결점으로 건강한 편은 아니에요 근데 저희 언니는 그런적도 없고 교우관계도 좋고 진짜 정신이 건강하거든요 ㅠ 근데 저희 언니가 그런말을 들었다니깐 진짜 도청이 일어나는게 맞는거구나 생각했어요.. 그리고 또 있었던 일을 말씀드리면 이동수업 때 제 뒷쪽에서 남자애가 제 아버지 직업을 언급하면서 제 이름을 말하는거에요 이게 도청을 하지 않고서는 절대 알수가 없는 사실이거든요 ㅠ 또 “정신병ㅋㅋㅋ” 하면서 제 이름을 언급하는거에요 이것도 도청을 하지 않았다면 알수 없는거고요 더 말씀드릴 사례가 많은데 그러면 너무 길어져서 이정도만 말씀드릴게요 그래서 찾아보니까 머리에 붙일수 있는 초소형 도청기가 있다길래  제 언니가 제 머리를 샅샅이 뒤져줬거든요? 근데 그래도 아무것도 안나오더라고요 ㅠ 그리고 또 도청 탐지 업체를 알아보니까 금액이 너무 비싸서요 ㅠ 제가 고3인데 이런일을 당해서 너무 스트레스 받는데 방법이 없어서 정말 어떻게 해야될지 모르겠어요 안그래도 제가 여자애들이나 남자애들이 괴롭힐 소재가 많은 조용한 애거든요 ㅠ그래서 저를 지나칠때 꼭 한마디 끼얹고 지나가고 그래서 학교생활이 막 편한 그런애는 아닌데 학교에서 유일하게 맘놓고 말할 수 있는 언니랑 말하는 얘기를 다 알고있으니까 스트레스 받아서 공부 능력도 점점 떨어지는것같고 쨋든 걱정이 이만저만이 아니에요 어떡해야되죠 ㅠㅠ 제가 성격이 활발한 편도 아니고 집에 돈이 많지도 않아서 진짜 대학 잘가야되는데 걱정이에요ㅠㅠ 긴글 읽어주셔서 감사하고요 여기가 사생활 침해 관련한 갤러리니까 혹여나 저랑 비슷한 경험이 있으시거나 관련 지식이 있는 분은 제가 어떻게 해야하는건지 알려주시면 진짜진짜 감사드릴것같아요 많은 도움 부탁드려요 정말 방법 여러가지 찾아봐도 안되겠어서 여기다 글 남겨요

Today, we’re rolling out Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, and making it generally available across the Gemini API and Gemini for business . Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash introduces native 15-second video creation, multi-turn conversational editing capabilities, and enhanced reference following. We have dropped the price 30% from Gemini Omni 1.1 making it available at $0.07 per second for 720p video.

Beyond the lower price, the workflow keeps costs down: you can draft fast at 360p or 720p, fix a detail with a follow-up edit instead of re-generating the entire clip, and then upscale your best creations to 1080p or 4K.

You can now generate and edit videos natively up to 15 seconds long, up from 10 seconds with Omni 1.1. You can also specify duration in one-second increments from 3 to 15 seconds, giving you room to tell complete stories, create product explainers, or produce full social ad spots in a single generation.

You can guide generation combining character, product, or style images, short motion clips (up to three seconds), and audio cues — and Omni 1.2 Flash holds onto those details from start to finish. Faces, garments, packaging typography, and brand colors stay consistent across camera angles, making it easy to turn existing product photography or character sheets into virtual try-on clips, catalog spins, and branded video ads.

Combining one model photo with front-and-back product shots of three outfits, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generates a 15-second virtual try-on sequence across 360-degree turns and match cuts while keeping the model’s identity and each garment’s cut, drape, and back details consistent.

You can maintain stronger character, object, and scene consistency from the first to the last frame, with less visual drift or morphing across motion and camera transitions. Whether you’re interpolating between a first and last keyframe, or extending a clip to build a longer sequence, products, characters, props, and environments stay consistent from shot to shot.

Given the same static studio lighting exhibition poster and five-layer animation prompt, Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash does not match the reference image as closely as 1.2 does. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash builds the poster sequentially layer by layer on the dusty-pink cyclorama rising the hexagonal plinth, assembling the ribbed glass, warm filament, faceted crystal, and coiled-cord letterforms for HALO, GLOW, and LUMEN, and locking every material, shadow, and typographic detail consistently through the final frame.

You can refine the same clip turn by turn — such as swapping a product or background, changing the lighting or weather, or switching the aspect ratio —…

items.title: What are you doing this weekend?
items.summary: ask, programming
items.content:
Feel free to tell what you plan on doing this weekend and even ask for help or feedback.

Please keep in mind it’s more than OK to do nothing at all too!

I will be implementing the hardness setting in the brush engine of my painting software. At the moment I only support importing predefined textures and this setting would allow a user to create an airbrush dynamically during runtime.

(It's a very standard feature but just happened to be implemented after texture stamping since it was easier to test the shaders in that order)

An art fair tomorrow night, then on Sunday hosting Zig Day Seattle: https://zig.day/usa/seattle/4/ All experience levels welcome. There's also one in Portland on Saturday, but I won't be at that one.

Also hopefully playing some Valheim. Recently started a new game with a couple others I played with when it was first in early access. Now we're playing the 1.0 release.

Looking at the stock market with excitement, hoping the current bubble not only pops, but explodes, making as much damage as possible.

Painful time to be a small-time investor. I'm sure other companies will pick up the slack once the market normalizes, but it's not pleasant seeing my savings drop by a thousand euros overnight. (Which might not be big money in a more Western country, but it sure is here.)

Oh well, as long as it cools the fad and forces a bit more rationality...

Planning my move from a corporate OS built on increasingly brittle foundations to a community project built on something a bit more solid

I've seen a lot of this sentiment recently, but Linux has never felt more stable to me than nowadays. It's actually so stable it's "boring" (which is not a bad thing, but it's definitely not a statement I would've made 15-20 years ago, doubly so while running an NVIDIA card).

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: Interpolative Software
items.content:
Much of the excitement around AI coding is downstream of the fact that a lot of

software is interpolative . This has become especially true as of late, with

the release of Opus 5.5, which is, I’d argue, superhumanly good at generating

mass amounts of high-quality interpolative software. 1

This post is mostly a reference post for an idea that I’ve been gesturing to

In 2026, software falls on a spectrum between interpolative software and novel

The vast majority of the software that most SWEs write 2 , most of the time, is

interpolative software . Interpolative software is code that is solidly

within the training distribution of models. Sometimes this means that the agents

were (likely) literally trained on examples of building pieces of software

(e.g., “build a todo app”, “build a clone of xyz.com”), or building within

particular APIs (e.g., React). Other times, the software “rhymes” with enough

existing software, or exists in a well-defined position between two pieces of

software, such that the model is able to interpolate between similar examples

Interpolative software can often be specified with just a few sentences of

prompting. The question to ask with respect to whether software is interpolative

or not is: how many bits of information do you have to include in your prompt to

get what you want? 3 If the answer is small, it’s interpolative. 4

Things like issue trackers, web forms, training pipelines, CI systems, workflow

engines, and pretty much anything that has a canonical reference design in the

Open Source literature will fall somewhat under this interpolative distinction.

On the other end of the spectrum, there’s novel software. One develops novel

software when making something that has fundamentally not existed before. This

is usually because either the constituent components do not exist in the

training distribution for agents, or they’re being combined in such a novel way

that agents’ intuition for how to assemble the components is insufficient to

solve the problem without significant human guidance.

Writing novel software with agents feels like “fighting uphill” because there

are enough novel components that you’re not pulling from a training corpus, and

the model is struggling to grok what you want. Not a lot of software is novel.

And this is fine; there’s a ton of value in the interpolative stuff.

At work, we’ve been redeveloping a large-scale distributed system that has a

complex set of specific requirements. I’m sure that a system that satisfies this

specific set of criteria has not existed in any company before. (And if it has,

it’s definitely not public, nor in any public training set.) It’s been

fascinating to watch coworkers push on this system for the better part of a

year, using copious amounts of agents and tokens. Despite it being one of the

most agent-pilled projects I’ve yet seen, it still requires a large amount of

diligent human shepherding to ensure that the system actually performs as

On the other hand, you can give an agent instructions of essentially “build

Anki” or “build Linear” and it’ll just do it end-to-end. I’ve done both of these

– I had agents rebuild large chunks of Anki into a personal set of tools. It

only took a few prompts, and was a complete no-op drop-in replacement for all

the features of Anki that I cared about. Ditto Linear. 5

What counts as interpolative software expands over time as

The AI industry sometimes measures this with task time horizon (e.g., the

METR time horizon graph ). This is a useful

metric, but it’s a proxy for, roughly, “what level of technical challenge can

you give to an agent and still have it produce something useful at the end”. The

amount of creative interpolation that agents can do is increasing – and at the

limit, sufficiently general, creative, extrapolative combinations of existing

components begin to look like novel inventions.

items.title_ko: ‘보간형 소프트웨어(Interpolative Software)’ 개념과 AI 코딩의 관계
items.summary_ko: 글쓴이는 AI 코딩에 대한 열기의 상당 부분이 대부분의 소프트웨어가 보간형(interpolative)이라는 사실에서 나온다고 주장한다. 보간형 소프트웨어는 모델의 학습 분포 안에 있는 코드를 뜻하며, Opus 5.5가 이런 소프트웨어를 대량으로 생성하는 데 매우 뛰어나다고 평가했다. 글은 2026년의 소프트웨어가 보간형과 novel 소프트웨어 사이의 스펙트럼에 놓인다는 관점을 설명하는 참고 글이다.

items.title: Upgrading NetBSD from 11.0 to 11.1
items.summary: netbsd
items.content:
I successfully upgraded my NetBSD amd64 system (with one hiccup, detailed below) from 11.0 to 11.1:

NetBSD 11.1 (GENERIC) #0: Mon Nov 2 16:34:32 UTC 2026 mkrepro@mkrepro.NetBSD.org:/usr/src/sys/arch/amd64/compile/GENERIC

This was my first time upgrading NetBSD and I’m happy with how it all turned out!

NetBSD’s Guide describes two different methods for performing an upgrade: boot from NetBSD install media and use sysinst(8) , or use sysupgrade(8) to do an in-place upgrade of the system. With a bit of research, I get the sense that for major version changes (i.e 10.1 -> 11.1) sysinst is the preferred method, while sysupgrade is a convenient alternative for minor version bumps.

So sysupgrade it is. First, I install the package:

# sysupgrade auto https://cdn.netbsd.org/pub/NetBSD/NetBSD-11.1/$(uname -m)/

This will proceed to download the kernel and sets appropriate for your computer, unpack them, then prompt you to review and merge new configuration changes. There were only a few files that needed hands-on editing like passwd and sshd_config and I liked how NetBSD shows the diffs between the old and new files and its handling of merging differences.

I had one postinstall check that failed:

# postinstall checks failed: opensslcertsrehash

I resolved the issue by wiping the legacy cache, then letting certctl(8) take over by rehasing the certs:

Verify certctl successfully populated the directory:

I manually re-run postinstall fix [issue] and confirm that it now passes inspection (which it did):

# sysupgrade postinstall fix opensslcertsrehash

Reboot the computer and start enjoying the upgrade!

In addition, edit /usr/pkg/etc/pkgin/repositories.conf and point pkgin to the new 11.1 repositories.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: Nvidia wants to repurpose over 130 old telco buildings as tiny data centers, report claims — company in talks with Brightspeed after pitching idea to parent company Apollo Global Management.
items.content:
Internet and telecommunications provider Brightspeed is reportedly in talks with Nvidia to convert several of its buildings into tiny data centers. According to The Information , Nvidia pitched the idea to Apollo Global Management executives, the parent company of Brightspeed, who then asked it to submit written plans to the internet provider. Nvidia complied and has now requested additional information, data, and site visits to some of Brightspeed’s existing infrastructure.

Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers

America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the price

GTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this year

Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible

The telecommunications company has around 130 buildings located around the country, many of which are already built to handle data and voice traffic and have the required power infrastructure to run Nvidia servers. Sources say that the AI tech giant estimates that these sites could collectively deliver around 1 gigawatt of compute capacity, which could accommodate more than 2,200 Supermicro Vera Rubin NVL72 racks containing 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs each. Although these sites already can power these GPUs, it’s still not a plug-and-play solution, as Nvidia would still need to install cooling systems and other supporting architecture. These would still require permits and approval from the local government, but they would likely face less red tape and opposition compared to building a data center from the ground up.

Apollo Global Management has already made significant bets in AI hardware, with the asset management company involved in a $40 billion deal with SpaceX that would give it around 360,000 Vera Rubin GPUs across 5,000 NVL72 racks. While it’s currently unclear who will own the AI chips installed in Brightspeed facilities, the proposal could potentially help Apollo find a place for the Nvidia chips it ordered to get them up and running as soon as possible. This is a much better solution compared to waiting for years to get a data center approved, all while facing resistance from the community even after getting the go-ahead from the local government.

Having multiple small data centers like this is also a setup that OpenAI and Anthropic have been considering , especially as larger facilities are facing delays and backlash from the communities that they’re in. While having a large, homogeneous cluster built in one location is preferable for training, Nvidia representatives have described these smaller sites working together as an “inference network” to help run existing AI models. This is especially important as AI agents, which use five to ten times more tokens than humans, become more popular.

The move to use existing facilities instead of building new ones from scratch has received renewed attention, especially after Americans overwhelmingly voted against data centers during the midterm elections. While the more than 300 data center bans enacted across the U.S. have only delayed three existing projects , it’s feared that the bans and moratoriums would make it that much harder to start new data center developments and make it difficult for AI companies to secure the compute capacity needed to power their AI models in the future.

items.title: Rana hainan, Hainan groove-toed frog from China
items.content:
New Frog Species Hidden on Hainan Island Gets a Name

A new species of frog has been formally described from Hainan Island in southern China. The animal, named Rana hainan and nicknamed the Hainan Groove-toed Frog, was identified from twelve specimens collected in the Shangxi Provincial Nature Reserve in Wanning City and on Mt. Diaoluo in Lingshui County. Researchers from Hainan Normal University, Shenyang Normal University and Sun Yat-sen University combined DNA sequencing with detailed body measurements to show that the Hainan frogs form a lineage that is clearly separate from their closest relatives on the mainland.

The discovery matters because Hainan’s frogs have carried a string of different scientific names since the 1970s. Liu and colleagues first reported a frog from Mt. Jianfengling in 1973 that they tentatively called Rana varians, flagging their own uncertainty with a question mark. Dubois later moved Chinese populations of that species into Rana nigrotympanica, and subsequent surveys expanded the taxon’s supposed Hainan range to sites including Mt. Jianfengling, Danzhou, Dongfang, Baisha, Tunchang, Qiongzhong, Mt. Diaoluo and Mt. Wuzhi. In 2007, Wang and colleagues confirmed the frog’s presence on the island using newly collected specimens from Mt. Diaoluo. Two years later, Fei and colleagues added Rana johnsi to the Hainan herpetofauna, and in 2011 Shi and colleagues reassigned the same Mt. Diaoluo specimens to Rana johnsi while also adding a record from Mt. Yinggeling.

That shifting history left the island’s brown frogs in taxonomic limbo. The new study, published in the journal ZooKeys, argues that the Mt. Diaoluo animals were never Rana johnsi at all. Instead, they belong to a distinct species within the Rana johnsi group of the subgenus Rana, a lineage defined by lateroventral grooves on the flattened toe tips and a triangular black patch on the temporal region. The researchers collected their specimens between January 2024 and April 2026 from montane tropical rainforest, euthanized them with the anesthetic MS-222, fixed them in buffered formalin and preserved them in ethanol, depositing the vouchers at three Chinese institutions.

To test whether the Hainan frogs were truly different, the team turned to genetics. They amplified three mitochondrial markers: partial 16S ribosomal RNA, the COI gene and cytochrome b. Combined with sequences downloaded from GenBank, the final dataset spanned 2,515 base pairs from 99 individuals across 44 species, with Rana shuchinae serving as the outgroup. Bayesian Inference and Maximum Likelihood analyses produced identical topologies. All samples of the Rana johnsi group formed a strongly supported monophyletic clade, and within it the Hainan population emerged as a distinct, well-supported lineage, with a Bayesian posterior probability of 1.00, an SH-aLRT value of 96.5 and an ultrafast bootstrap support of 96. That lineage sits as sister to the clade containing R. johnsi, R. wuyiensis and R. sangzhiensis.

The genetic distances were substantial. Using Kimura 2-parameter distances, the Hainan lineage diverged from all recognized congeners in the analysis by 1.50 to 10.85 percent at 16S, 5.90 to 20.09 percent at COI and 7.37 to 21.29 percent at cytochrome b. The phylogeny also revealed a clear geographic structure: R. johnsi ranges from central Vietnam to Guangxi in southern China, R. sangzhiensis occurs mainly in central and southwestern China including Hunan and Sichuan, and R. wuyiensis is restricted to the Wuyi Mountains of Fujian. Each lineage occupies a separate montane region, a disjunct pattern that the authors suggest points to geographic isolation as an important driver of diversification in the group.

Morphology told the same story. Because females were scarce, the statistical analyses used only males: three from Hainan, ten R. johnsi, 27 R. sangzhiensis and four R. wuyiensis. Seventeen measurements, from snout-vent length to tibia width, were log-transformed and…

items.summary_ko: 하이난 섬에서 발견된 개구리 신종 Rana hainan(하이난 홈발가락 개구리)이 공식 기재됐다. 완안성 샹시 자연보호구와 디아오뤄산 등에서 채집된 표본 12점을 바탕으로, DNA 염기서열 분석과 신체 측정을 함께 활용해 본토의 가까운 종과 뚜렷이 구분되는 계통임을 확인했다. 하이난의 개구리는 1970년대 이후 여러 학명으로 불리며 분류가 혼란스러웠던 것으로 전해진다.
items.content_ko: 하이난섬 남부에서 발견된 개구리 신종이 학명으로 공식 기재됐다. 이름은 Rana hainan이며, 별명은 하이난 홈발가락 개구리(Hainan Groove-toed Frog)다. 완닝시 샹시 성급 자연보호구와 링수이현 디아오뤄산에서 채집한 표본 12개를 근거로 했다. 하이난사범대, 선양사범대, 중산대 연구진이 DNA 염기서열 분석과 상세한 신체 측정을 함께 사용해 하이난 개구리가 본토의 가장 가까운 친척과 명확히 구분되는 계통임을 보였다. 하이난 개구리는 1970년대 이후 여러 이름으로 불려 왔다. 1973년 Liu 등은 지펑링산 개구리를 Rana varians로 잠정 보고하면서 물음표로 불확실성을 표시했다. 이후 Dubois가 중국 개체군을 Rana nigrotympanica로 옮겼고, 여러 조사에서 이 분류군의 하이난 분포지가 확장됐다. 2007년 Wang 등의 연구가 이어졌으나, 원문이 중간에서 끝나 최종 결론의 세부 내용은 확인되지 않았다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: A Jev that can ask Opus for help gives Opus accuracy at 4x lower cost
items.content:
We wanted to test whether LLMs and decision models, specifically Jev and Luna, could solve a hard problem that we encounter regularly (grading identity resolution results). We found that while both models performed okay out of the box (88.8–97.3% accuracy), implementing a hybrid model that combines Jev + Opus achieves frontier accuracy at > 4x lower costs.

Luna performs better than Jev out of the box, but the gap disappears on harder cases.

Jev's confidence is better calibrated. Most of its mistakes come with low confidence its right. Most of Luna's mistakes come with high confidence. This enables Jev to perform better than Luna in a hybrid model harness.

Frontier models are still more accurate than decision models

Decision models are up to 90× cheaper and more than 10× faster out of the box. They cost $0.5 - $0.10 per 1,000 identities and answer in about 0.15 seconds, but trail Opus accuracy by about 6 percentage points on harder benchmarks.

Identity resolution is the process of mapping data to corresponding real people. More precisely, say you have a set of data records D . Determine a set of identities I and mapping m(D)->I such that each record d ∈ D maps to an identity i ∈ I , each i corresponds to exactly one real person in the real world, and no two i correspond to the same person in the real world.

This is foundational for any company wishing to do outreach, personalization, or analytics on customers. You can’t know, for instance, the lifetime value of a customer without being able to map all their purchases to a single identity.

For example, the input data might contain the following records. IDR would ideally create one identity, Alice , and associate all of these records with Alice .

Name Email Home address Shipping address

loyalty_record_1 Alice alice@alice.com — —

transaction_record_1 Alice — — 123 Main St

transaction_record_2 (null) alice@alice.com — Store Pickup

In practice, IDR is very difficult. People share emails, move addresses, etc. There might also be errors in the data. See some examples here:

Error Type What it looks like What it could also mean

Typo Valentino → Valentinp A different surname

Misread character Sam → 5am Garbage, or a username

Spelled how it sounds Phillips → Filips A different family

Month and day swapped 02/17/2020 → 17/02/2020 A birth date that doesn’t parse

Value copied from a relative A child listed with a parent’s birth date An adult with the child’s name

Placeholder name Valentino → Female Child Nothing useful at all

The most common and problematic issue with IDR is over-merging . This is when an identity i incorrectly corresponds to multiple people in the real world.

On real data, there is no answer key we can consult after we’ve merged records into identities. If there were, then we'd just use that to match data, and we wouldn't need to do IDR. This makes it very difficult to assess the accuracy of any IDR algorithm. In practice, teams will spend months attempting to determine if their IDR is working.

You can use heuristics to look for statistical signs of over-merged profiles (count the number of emails per identity, etc), but ultimately you need to sample output identities and review them by hand to know how well your IDR algorithm is performing.

To do this, we define the records Dᵢ as the set of d such that m(d) -> i for any given i . If the IDR engine is successful, then we should only find evidence of one real person in any given Dᵢ .

Human sampling is slow (~50 identities/hr), and sampling small numbers of identities gives poor estimates of over-merging. Over-merges are rare in a healthy graph, and estimating a rare rate precisely takes more samples than people expect (> 1000 samples to get the error down to under +-1% on over-merging rate)

An LLM should, intuitively, be able to replicate what a human is doing when they inspect an identity. If a model can judge identities at human accuracy, then we could spin up as many LLMs as we want to grade…
items.title_ko: Jev가 Opus에 도움을 요청하는 하이브리드 구조로 Opus 수준 정확도를 4배 이상 낮은 비용에 구현
items.summary_ko: 신원 식별(identity resolution) 결과를 채점하는 문제에서 Jev와 Luna 같은 모델을 테스트했다. 두 모델은 기본 상태로도 88.8~97.3%의 정확도를 보였고, Jev와 Opus를 결합한 하이브리드 모델은 최상위급 정확도를 4배 넘게 낮은 비용으로 달성했다. 결정 모델은 기본 상태로 최대 90배 저렴하고 10배 이상 빠르지만, 어려운 벤치마크에서는 Opus보다 약 6%p 낮은 정확도를 보인다.
items.content_ko: 연구진은 데이터 레코드를 실제 사람에 대응시키는 신원 식별 문제, 즉 결과를 채점하는 작업에서 LLM과 결정 모델(decision model)인 Jev와 Luna를 시험했다. 두 모델은 기본 상태에서 88.8~97.3%의 정확도를 보였다. Luna는 기본 상태에서 Jev보다 성능이 좋았지만, 어려운 사례에서는 그 차이가 사라졌다. Jev의 신뢰도는 더 잘 보정되어 있어, 틀린 답의 대부분이 낮은 신뢰도를 동반했다. 반면 Luna의 오류 대부분은 높은 신뢰도를 동반했다. 이 때문에 하이브리드 구조에서는 Jev가 Luna보다 나은 성능을 냈다. 프런티어 모델은 여전히 결정 모델보다 정확하다. 결정 모델은 기본 상태에서 최대 90배 저렴하고 10배 이상 빠르며, 1,000개 식별자당 비용은 원문 기준 $0.5~$0.10 수준이고 응답 시간은 약 0.15초다. 다만 어려운 벤치마크에서는 Opus 정확도보다 약 6%p 낮았다. 하이브리드 구조는 Jev가 Opus에 도움을 요청하는 방식으로 Opus 수준 정확도를 4배 넘게 낮은 비용으로 달성했다고 소개됐다.

why did nobody notice? well, maybe someone did. maybe someone pasted the wrong thing into a password prompt, half a slack message or a whole ssh key, and it just let them in. you've never pasted the wrong thing into a password prompt?? amazing. a fresh box with no passwords set isn't affected. a * in shadow needs a wrong try first. openssh tests on openbsd and glibc, musl doesn't test sshd, and most distros go through pam, which never even calls crypt for a * .

so as far as anyone knows, nobody noticed. as far as anyone knows.

items.title_ko: sshhole: OpenSSH의 '*' 암호 필드 처리 문제를 추적한 기록
items.summary_ko: 작성자는 sshd에서 '*' 암호 필드를 처리하는 방식과 관련된 문제를 정리했다. glibc, musl, libxcrypt 사이의 처리 차이가 핵심 쟁점으로 제시된다. 작성자는 OpenSSH의 pick_salt() 수정 코드에서 네 줄 아래에 해당 버그가 있다고 주장한다.
items.content_ko: 작성자는 sshd 관련 문제를 설명한다. 비밀번호 입력란에 잘못된 값(슬랙 메시지 일부나 SSH 키 전체)이 들어가 로그인이 되는 경우가 있었을 수 있다고 추정한다. 비밀번호가 설정되지 않은 새 시스템은 영향을 받지 않는다고 적는다. OpenSSH 테스트는 OpenBSD와 glibc에서 수행되고 musl은 sshd를 테스트하지 않으며, 대부분의 배포판은 PAM을 거쳐 '*'에 대해 crypt를 호출하지 않는다고 설명한다. 2013년 Debian 개발자가 glibc에 musl의 '*' 처리 방식을 따르도록 요청했지만, 이후 Debian은 libxcrypt로 옮겨가며 이 버그를 닫았다. libxcrypt는 '*0'을 사용한다. 2024년 musl 메일링 리스트에서는 257자 비밀번호에서 busybox passwd가 깨지는 문제가 논의됐으며, 같은 '*'와 같은 길이 한계가 관련된다. 2026년 10월 OpenSSH 커밋에서 보안 검토로 pick_salt()가 수정됐고, 그 버그는 수정 코드에서 네 줄 아래에 있었다. 이 수정은 작성자가 버그를 발견하기 나흘 전에 이루어졌다고 적혀 있다. 작성자는 지금까지 아무도 이 문제를 알아채지 못한 것으로 알려져 있다고 쓴다.

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: How Video Recordings are locatable by whoever puts the effort
items.content:
Aircraft sounds in background audio can leave traces that help identify where a video was recorded.

Colsto says matching those sound traces with flight data can triangulate a location within about 100 meters.

The method is complex, and Colsto says easier ways to find someone still exist.

Livestreamers, journalists, creators, and whistleblowers face higher risk when they need to hide their location.

Key Takeaways by nexos.ai , reviewed by Cybernews staff.

Security researcher and YouTuber Colsto has demonstrated how seemingly ordinary background audio can reveal where a video was recorded.

The technique relies on the Doppler effect, the phenomenon that makes sirens sound like they change pitch as they move towards or away from you.

Colsto discovered that aircraft can leave identifiable acoustic traces in recordings, even when they are inaudible to the person recording or watching the video.

Researchers can determine the direction an aircraft was traveling by measuring the Doppler effect and matching the pattern to aircraft tracking data.

Landlords put AI behind Ring cameras to monitor guests: count visitors, detect parties, and other house rule violations

X has started tracking what you share. But you can do something about it

Zuckerberg under the spotlight over privacy - will anything change this time?

GM settles claims over sharing drivers’ location and behavior data with insurers

French privacy watchdog fines FNAC €7M for tracking app users without consent

UK privacy watchdog reprimands police over victim’s exposed address

Combining multiple aircraft signatures creates enough reference points to triangulate the recording location, with an apparent accuracy rate of within 100 meters. The researcher added that no visual cues are necessary.

Audio processing during video upload and noise-reduction techniques are not enough to remove the aircraft residue.

Colsto was keen to point out that his video was for educational purposes, and not to promote fear. The idea is to raise awareness of open-source intelligence (using publicly available recordings and matching them with other publicly available information to reveal something private).

Importantly, Colsto acknowledged that the technique is complicated and unlikely to become an everyday tracking method overnight, saying:

There's probably a hundred easier ways to find you than this.

Who could be exposed, and could anything be done?

One of the biggest potential problems is the threat to individuals who desire to conceal their locations. That intention is common amongst livestreamers, independent journalists, content creators, and whistleblowers.

While photographs can be stripped of identifying metadata or framed to hide surroundings, audio recordings contain elements that can bypass the broadcaster.

On Reddit, the vulnerability was explored further with one commenter speculating that it’s “surprisingly hard to protect against.”

One reply advised denoising the audio to “remove low volume sounds” to bolster one's privacy. Basic programs like Audacity or SimpleClean offer this service.
